title: Pseudobulk differential expression with DESeq2
text: Single cells donor statistically independent: share genetic background, batch effects, ambient RNA. Treating cell independent observation regression inflates effective sample size distorts p-values. common, principled remedy pseudobulk: sum donor’s cells within group (e.g. cluster) produce per-donor count vector, run count-based regression like DESeq2::DESeq donors. unit replication becomes donor, cell. presto provides: collapse_counts() — fast collapse cell--gene count matrix pseudobulks defined one metadata columns. pseudobulk_deseq2() — run DESeq2 across resulting pseudobulks one-vs-, pairwise, within-group design. top_markers_dds() — extract top features per group result.

title: Pseudobulk differential expression with DESeq2
text: use colon-tissue CD8 T-cell dataset Thomas et al. Nat. Med. 2024 (GSE206299). 27 donors, 9 cell clusters, 25,341 cells. crosstab confirms donors contribute cells clusters — good news pseudobulk, since clusters represented donors low statistical power.

title: Pseudobulk differential expression with DESeq2
text: collapse_counts() sums columns count matrix according one metadata columns. collapse (donor, cluster), drop (donor, cluster) pair fewer 10 cells, keep cell count N can inspect came . collapse (donor, cluster, case) instead just (donor, cluster) case constant within donor — including now makes available within-cluster contrast Step 4. cc$counts_mat now 28,165-gene × 204-pseudobulk matrix. column one (donor, cluster) sample; cc$meta_data matching data.frame pseudobulk identities.
code: md <- data.frame(     donor   = as.character(d$obs$donor),     cluster = as.character(d$obs$cluster),     case    = as.character(d$obs$case),     stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) cc <- collapse_counts(     d$counts, md, c("donor", "cluster", "case"),     min_cells_per_group = 10,     keep_n = TRUE ) dim(cc$counts_mat) #> [1] 28165   204 head(cc$meta_data) #>   donor cluster    case   N #> 1  MC_1       5 Control  80 #> 2  MC_1       3 Control  46 #> 3  MC_1       4 Control 100 #> 4  MC_1       1 Control 323 #> 5  MC_1       6 Control  51 #> 6  MC_1       2 Control 110 table(cc$meta_data$cluster) #>  #>  1  2  3  4  5  6  7  8  9  #> 27 27 26 27 25 23 26 18  5

title: Pseudobulk differential expression with DESeq2
text: pseudobulk_deseq2() mode = "one_vs_all" tests cluster union others. collapse_background = FALSE keep background pseudobulk observation; setting TRUE collapses background pseudobulks per donor first, preferable donors unbalanced across clusters. first variable formula contrast variable. meta_data contain pseudobulk identifying variables used formula. Result columns come straight DESeq2::results(), prepended group identifier:
code: md_dge <- cc$meta_data[, "cluster", drop = FALSE] res <- pseudobulk_deseq2(     ~cluster, md_dge, cc$counts_mat,     verbose = FALSE,     min_counts_per_sample = 10,     present_in_min_samples = 5,     collapse_background = FALSE,     mode = "one_vs_all" ) head(res) #>   group                  feature baseMean log2FoldChange lfcSE stat   pvalue     padj #> 1     1      ENSG00000128951|DUT    42.72           1.35 0.108 12.5 6.67e-36 6.69e-32 #> 2     1     ENSG00000105486|LIG1     4.18           1.69 0.138 12.2 2.49e-34 1.25e-30 #> 3     1 ENSG00000134291|TMEM106C    13.14           1.67 0.138 12.1 7.54e-34 2.52e-30 #> 4     1    ENSG00000188486|H2AFX    10.49           1.86 0.155 12.0 2.92e-33 7.33e-30 #> 5     1     ENSG00000120802|TMPO    14.95           1.34 0.113 11.9 1.13e-32 2.27e-29 #> 6     1     ENSG00000163535|SGO2     2.85           2.17 0.186 11.7 1.50e-31 2.50e-28

title: Pseudobulk differential expression with DESeq2
text: mode = "pairwise" tests cluster cluster individually, returning long-form table group1 group2 columns. conservative one-vs-true marker differentiate cluster every cluster, just average background. cost grows quickly — N clusters means N × (N−1) directional DESeq2 fits — ’s worth subsetting levels care first. contrast clusters 1, 2, 3: summarize_dge_pairs() collapses directional pairs one row per (group, gene). Pass "min" keep gene’s worst comparison (conservative effect, useful high-confidence markers) "max" best.

title: Pseudobulk differential expression with DESeq2
text: interesting biological question “defines cluster” “cluster, genes change irColitis cases healthy controls?”. mode = "within" answers . first variable formula split variable (cluster), second contrast variable (case). Within level split variable, DESeq2 fits inner formula (~case). Top genes upregulated cases per cluster: Cluster-1 cases -regulate NCF1, PRNP, TXNIP — interferon-response oxidative-stress genes consistent inflamed tissue.
code: md_w <- cc$meta_data[, c("cluster", "case")]  res_w <- pseudobulk_deseq2(     ~cluster + case, md_w, cc$counts_mat,     verbose = FALSE,     min_counts_per_sample = 10,     present_in_min_samples = 5,     mode = "within" ) head(res_w) #>   group                   feature baseMean log2FoldChange lfcSE stat   pvalue     padj #> 1     1      ENSG00000158517|NCF1    73.62           1.45 0.194 7.50 6.58e-14 3.38e-11 #> 2     1      ENSG00000171867|PRNP    30.67           1.80 0.242 7.45 9.11e-14 4.45e-11 #> 3     1     ENSG00000162496|DHRS3     8.52           2.62 0.386 6.77 1.29e-11 4.51e-09 #> 4     1      ENSG00000185101|ANO9    10.32           1.76 0.261 6.75 1.52e-11 4.63e-09 #> 5     1     ENSG00000265972|TXNIP   202.85           1.34 0.199 6.74 1.60e-11 4.74e-09 #> 6     1 ENSG00000268804|LINC02132     9.84           2.78 0.414 6.72 1.78e-11 4.99e-09 top_markers_dds(res_w, n = 5, padj_max = 1e-4, lfc_min = 1) %>%     dplyr::mutate(across(-rank, ~ sub(".*\\|", "", .x))) #> # A tibble: 5 × 9 #>    rank `1`   `2`    `3`   `4`   `5`    `6`    `7`     `8`    #>   <int> <chr> <chr>  <chr> <chr> <chr>  <chr>  <chr>   <chr>  #> 1     1 NCF1  SPINK2 LAIR1 DHRS7 SPINK2 GNPTAB LDLRAD4 RPS12  #> 2     2 PRNP  SORBS3 <NA>  CA10  <NA>   DHRS7  <NA>    RPL30  #> 3     3 DHRS3 KIFC3  <NA>  NCF1  <NA>   TXNIP  <NA>    EEF1B2 #> 4     4 ANO9  GNPTAB <NA>  KIFC3 <NA>   FCER1G <NA>    MT-ND3 #> 5     5 TXNIP CALHM6 <NA>  MYBL1 <NA>   TGFBR1 <NA>    <NA>

title: Pseudobulk differential expression with DESeq2
text: Filter low-count genes early. min_counts_per_sample present_in_min_samples applied fitting; tighter filters speed DESeq2 step substantially. Always include batch / channel covariates possible. Add formula contrast variable (e.g. ~cluster + channel) design supports . collapse_background = TRUE (mode = "one_vs_all") can stabilize results donor representation uneven across clusters. mode = "within" supports 2-level ordinal contrasts. Two-level contrasts (factor character) get Wald test level-vs-reference coefficient. Three levels integer-encoded treated ordinal trend.

code: library(presto)  ## Generate a tiny toy dataset deterministically. set.seed(42) exprs <- matrix(rpois(25 * 150, lambda = 2), nrow = 25,                 dimnames = list(paste0("G", 1:25), NULL)) y <- rep(c("A", "B", "C"), each = 50)  res <- wilcoxauc(exprs, y) head(res) #>   feature group avgExpr  logFC statistic   auc   pval  padj pct_in pct_out #> 1      G1     A    2.10  0.200      2740 0.548 0.3264 0.510     86      89 #> 2      G2     A    1.58 -0.560      1896 0.379 0.0137 0.172     84      86 #> 3      G3     A    1.86  0.020      2432 0.486 0.7826 0.893     84      89 #> 4      G4     A    1.96 -0.210      2384 0.477 0.6362 0.884     90      90 #> 5      G5     A    2.00 -0.280      2214 0.443 0.2442 0.505     82      88 #> 6      G6     A    2.26  0.240      2775 0.555 0.2627 0.505     90      83 top_markers(res, n = 5, auc_min = 0.5) #> # A tibble: 5 × 4 #>    rank A     B     C #>   <int> <chr> <chr> <chr> #> 1     1 G10   G15   G25 #> 2     2 G24   G13   G5 #> 3     3 G16   G22   G18 #> 4     4 G6    G2    G14 #> 5     5 G7    G20   G2 wilcoxauc(seurat_object, group_by = "cluster") wilcoxauc(sce_object,    group_by = "cluster")

title: Collapse a single-cell count matrix into pseudobulks — collapse_counts
text: Sums (averages) columns feature--cell count matrix according one cell-metadata columns. result feature--pseudobulk matrix column pools cells share combination metadata values (e.g. cells given donor given cluster). resulting matrix suitable bulk-RNA-seq tools DESeq2, edgeR, limma. See pseudobulk vignette end--end walkthrough.

title: Collapse a single-cell count matrix into pseudobulks — collapse_counts
code: collapse_counts(   counts_mat,   meta_data,   varnames,   min_cells_per_group = 0,   keep_n = FALSE,   how = c("sum", "mean")[1] )

title: Collapse a single-cell count matrix into pseudobulks — collapse_counts
text: counts_mat Counts matrix. Rows features (genes), columns cells. Sparse (dgCMatrix) dense. meta_data data.frame cell metadata. Must one row per column counts_mat. varnames Character vector column names meta_data together define pseudobulk grouping. unique combination values across columns becomes one pseudobulk sample. min_cells_per_group Drop pseudobulks containing fewer many cells. Default 0 (keep ). keep_n TRUE, retain per-pseudobulk cell count column N returned meta_data. Default FALSE. "sum" (default) sums counts across cells pseudobulk; "mean" divides N give mean expression per cell. DESeq2 count-based regressions expect sums.

title: Collapse a single-cell count matrix into pseudobulks — collapse_counts
text: list two elements: counts_mat - feature--pseudobulk numeric matrix. meta_data - data.frame one row per pseudobulk containing columns named varnames (N keep_n = TRUE).

title: Collapse a single-cell count matrix into pseudobulks — collapse_counts
code: m <- matrix(sample.int(8, 100*500, replace=TRUE), nrow=100, ncol=500) rownames(m) <- paste0("G", 1:100) colnames(m) <- paste0("C", 1:500) md1 <- sample(c("a", "b"), 500, replace=TRUE) md2 <- sample(c("c", "d"), 500, replace=TRUE) df <- data.frame(md1, md2) data_collapsed <- collapse_counts(m, df, c("md1", "md2")) head(data_collapsed$counts_mat) #>    sample_1 sample_0 sample_2 sample_3 #> G1      627      523      550      573 #> G2      663      498      559      554 #> G3      574      517      575      502 #> G4      605      511      551      520 #> G5      639      548      577      546 #> G6      582      554      596      521 head(data_collapsed$meta_data) #>   md1 md2 #> 1   b   c #> 2   a   c #> 3   a   d #> 4   b   d

what: Pseudobulk differential expression with DESeq2 — pseudobulk_deseq2
title: Pseudobulk differential expression with DESeq2 — pseudobulk_deseq2
text: Runs DESeq2::DESeq() feature--pseudobulk count matrix identify genes whose expression differs groups pseudobulks. Three test designs supported, selected mode: "one_vs_all" (default) - test level contrast variable union others. Useful marker discovery. Dispatched pseudobulk_one_vs_all(). "pairwise" - test every ordered pair levels separately. Useful high-confidence markers; combine summarize_dge_pairs() keep conservative pair. Dispatched pseudobulk_pairwise(). "within" - split first term dge_formula test second term within split level. Useful condition / case-vs-control comparisons restricted one cluster time. Dispatched pseudobulk_within(). Pseudobulk inputs typically produced collapse_counts(). Genes low counts across pseudobulks filtered fitting (controlled min_counts_per_sample present_in_min_samples). See pseudobulk vignette end--end walkthrough real single-cell dataset.

what: Fast Wilcoxon rank-sum test and auROC across groups — wilcoxauc
title: Fast Wilcoxon rank-sum test and auROC across groups — wilcoxauc
text: every (feature, group) pair, computes Wilcoxon rank-sum statistic comparing observations group observations, area ROC curve measure separability. P-values come standard Gaussian approximation U statistic tie correction. Returns one row per (feature, group) effect-size percent-expressed columns alongside test statistics.

title: Fast Wilcoxon rank-sum test and auROC across groups — wilcoxauc
code: wilcoxauc(X, ...)  # S3 method for class 'seurat' wilcoxauc(X, ...)  # S3 method for class 'Seurat' wilcoxauc(   X,   group_by = NULL,   assay = "data",   groups_use = NULL,   seurat_assay = "RNA",   ... )  # S3 method for class 'SingleCellExperiment' wilcoxauc(X, group_by = NULL, assay = NULL, groups_use = NULL, ...)  # Default S3 method wilcoxauc(   X,   y,   groups_use = NULL,   verbose = TRUE,   nthreads = 1,   transposed = FALSE,   ... )

title: Fast Wilcoxon rank-sum test and auROC across groups — wilcoxauc
text: X Input data. One : numeric feature--observation matrix data.frame, sparse dgCMatrix shape, disk-backed DelayedMatrix (e.g. HDF5-backed, DelayedArray / HDF5Array packages), processed feature blocks whole matrix never loaded memory, matrix-like class (., "dgCMatrix") coercion method (e.g. BPCells), converted front, Seurat (v3+) object, SingleCellExperiment object. X must contain NA values. Unlike stats::wilcox.test(), drops missing values per observation, wilcoxauc() errors NA input rather returning silently incorrect results; remove impute missing values first. ... Passed input-specific method. group_by Seurat SingleCellExperiment input, name metadata column holds group labels (e.g. "cluster"). Seurat, defaults Idents(X). assay Seurat, layer name within selected assay (e.g. "data", "counts", "scale.data"). SingleCellExperiment, assay name (e.g. "logcounts", "counts"). Defaults pick sensible value per input class. groups_use Optional character vector restricting test subset groups y (group_by). Default NULL tests every group. seurat_assay Seurat input, name assay pull (e.g. "RNA"). Default "RNA". y matrix input, character/factor vector group labels length equal ncol(X). Ignored Seurat / SingleCellExperiment input (use group_by instead). verbose Logical. Print warnings informational messages. Default TRUE. nthreads Number threads per-feature ranking sparse (dgCMatrix) input. Default 1 (serial). Values 1 split ranking across threads; result identical regardless thread count. sparse input parallelized – dense matrix data.frame input always processed serially. running R CMD check CRAN, keep default two cores used. transposed Set TRUE observations (cells, samples) rows X features columns – .e. X transpose default features--observations layout. test runs directly layout without materializing transposed copy, saves time memory large matrices. convention transposed argument scater's calculatePCA() calculateUMAP(). applies matrix-like input (Seurat / SingleCellExperiment dispatchers always extract features--observations). Default FALSE.

title: Fast Wilcoxon rank-sum test and auROC across groups — wilcoxauc
text: table following columns: feature - feature name (e.g. gene name). group - group name. avgExpr - mean value feature group. logFC - difference mean feature values observations group vs group. input log-transformed expression (e.g. Seurat's "data" layer logcounts), difference means log fold change. raw (untransformed) values plain difference means, fold change. statistic - Wilcoxon rank sum U statistic. auc - area receiver operator curve. pval - nominal p value. padj - Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p value. pct_in - Percent observations group non-zero feature value. pct_out - Percent observations group non-zero feature value.

title: Fast Wilcoxon rank-sum test and auROC across groups — wilcoxauc
text: Designed fast enough run whole-genome × hundred-thousand- cell single-cell matrices seconds. Sparse dgCMatrix inputs processed without densification. Convenience dispatchers extract counts matrix group labels Seurat SingleCellExperiment objects. See getting-started vignette end--end example real dataset.

title: presto 1.1.0
text: wilcoxauc() accepts disk-backed DelayedMatrix input (e.g. HDF5-backed assays HDF5Array), processed feature blocks whole matrix never loaded memory (#26). matrix-like classes (., "dgCMatrix") method (e.g. BPCells) coerced automatically. wilcoxauc() gains transposed argument observations x features input (samples rows), runs directly layout without materializing transposed copy (#18). wilcoxauc() gains nthreads argument: per-feature ranking sparse (dgCMatrix) input can run multithreaded. Results identical thread count; roughly 2.6x faster 4 threads 3,000 x 80,000 matrix. default (nthreads = 1) unchanged. New toy_seurat() toy_sce() generate small example Seurat / SingleCellExperiment objects fly installed package versions, can never go stale. New load_ircolitis_cd8() downloads caches 25,341-cell colon CD8 T-cell dataset (GSE206299, Thomas et al. 2024) used vignettes. Two vignettes: Getting started presto Pseudobulk differential expression DESeq2, run real ircolitis dataset.

title: presto 1.1.0
text: wilcoxauc() now stops informative error X contains NA values, instead silently returning incorrect results (#25). shipped object_seurat object_sce datasets removed; use toy_seurat() toy_sce() instead. Rcpp data.table moved Depends Imports, longer attached search path presto loaded.

title: presto 1.1.0
text: Wilcoxon variance correction now includes every tie group: final tie group per feature implicit-zero group -zero features used dropped, inflating p-values heavily tied data (#29). P-values now agree stats::wilcox.test() machine precision; typical count data change tiny (< 1e-4), meaningful binary heavily tied features. Constant features report pval = 1 instead arbitrary value. wilcoxauc() rank_matrix() longer modify input place: dense input used silently overwritten ranks via aliased memory buffer (#7). Dense avgExpr logFC computed original values (also #7). Seurat dispatcher wilcoxauc() uses layer argument required Seurat 5 (#44). pseudobulk_within() handles character multi-level contrast variables. pseudobulk_pairwise() longer fails single-column meta_data. summarize_dge_pairs() longer prints debug output, pseudobulk_deseq2() longer warns unconditionally. Replaced deprecated .data$ tidyselect usage superseded tidyr::spread() tidyr::pivot_wider() top_markers() top_markers_dds() (#20).

title: presto 1.1.0
text: sparse-input statistics wilcoxauc() (transpose, ranking, group-wise reductions) fused single-pass C++ kernel, 12% faster serially threading.
